newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kremlin aide sees brief power transfer by Yeltsin.
newsitem.headline: Kremlin aide sees brief power transfer by Yeltsin.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin is likely to hand over power, including the "nuclear button", for a period of 10 hours to two days when he has heart surgery, an aide said in an interview published on Tuesday.

Anatoly Chubais, the Kremlin chief of staff, told the Izvestia newspaper that Yeltsin was expected to issue a decree handing his duties temporarily to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin just before he has surgery.
"It is a question of a document which will act perhaps for 10 hours or perhaps a day or two," Chubais said in the interview in the newspaper's Wednesday edition.
Asked if this would include handing over the "red button" which launches Russia's nuclear missiles, Chubais said: "Yes."
A council of doctors is due to convene on September 25 or 26 to decide when Yeltsin, 65, will have a bypass operation to improve the supply of blood to his heart.
Yeltsin has not confirmed he will give up his powers temporarily but his press secretary has said the president is considering various options for doing so.
The constitution says the prime minister should assume the president's duties temporarily if the head of state is incapacitated but Yeltsin has not formally named Chernomyrdin as his deputy.
The constitution does not stipluate how the transfer of power should take place.

"I think that at the moment the operation is to be undergone -- that is when the president cannot carry out his duties -- a presidential decree will appear legally defining how power is specifically transferred to the prime minsiter," Chubais said.
"Correspondingly, after the operation another decree will appear which will repeal the previous one."
